critical_operation.code_excerpt:
defp compare_host?(_request_host, nil),
    do: true
  defp compare_host?(request_host, "*." <> allowed_host),
    do: String.ends_with?(request_host, allowed_host)
  defp compare_host?(request_host, allowed_host),
    do: request_host == allowed_host
critical_operation.description: For a wildcard allowed origin such as `*.ex.com`, the pattern is stripped to `ex.com` and the request host is accepted when it merely ends with that string. No dot boundary is required, so `org1.prefix-ex.com` and `notex.com` style hosts pass the check even though they are not subdomains of ex.com. The fixed clause requires either an exact host match (`ex.com`) or a suffix preceded by a dot (`'.' <> allowed_host`), which forces the wildcard to match only real subdomains. The bug is reached from check_origin/2 via origin_allowed?/4 and compare_host?/2; the regression tests added in the fix reject `https://org1.prefix-ex.com` and `http://org1.prefix-foo.example.com`.

entry_point.description: The public check_origin/5 (defined with a default sender argument, usable as check_origin/4) reads the Origin header and calls origin_allowed?/4; that dispatches the configured list to origin_allowed?/2, which reaches compare_host?/2. No application-level validation sits between the header and the wildcard comparison.
